Low Pressure Heater 
out of Operation

Dismantle the 
 outer insulation for upper cover for Low pressure Heater.

Dismantle the screws of two flanges ( inlet and 
 outlet of water side ) .
Dismantle the studs of upper cover .

Remove the screws of two flanges and the studs 
 of upper cover to be cleaned .

sections.text: Lift the upper cover about 1 mm by using two depressing screws .
Remove the upper cover by using the main lift.
Test the leakage of tubes and mark the defected tubes.

Make a test to Low pressure Heater from steam side and then notice around the 
 welding tubes to the tubes plate from leakage.
Take the tube bundle out of the Low pressure Heater jacket.
Remove all the tubes which blinded.

Notice the level of any tubes of L. P. H. E for decreasing the level and set 
 the Coordinates of this tubes ( X , Y ) .
Check all parts for any worn-out and replace them by new ones.

sections.text:
Assembly the new tubes in the position of the defective tubes by beading and 
 welding.
Take the tube bundle in the Low pressure Heater jacket after cleaning it.

Make finally test for Low pressure Heater to insure no leakage happened in 
 tubes.
Put the gasket of upper cover Low pressure Heater.

Set the upper cover of Low pressure Heater carefully and notice the flanges of 
 inlet and outlet water side .

Put the flange gasket and tightening of the flanged joints ( cover and two 
 flanges of water side ) adhere to the uniform tighten cross wise , i.e 
 converted to a clock dial tighten in the sequence of 3-9-12-6 and then round 
 and round .
Excess stresses to the screws to the screws and studs .

After we put the Low pressure Heater to working operation about 24 hours we 
 retighten the screws of two flanges ( water side ) and studs of the cover .
